question.text: Given \(f(x)=e^{\sin x}+e^{\cos x}\). The global maximum value of \(f(x)\)

options.text: exists at a point in \(\left(0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\) and its value is \(2 e^{\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}}\)

solution.text:
Hint : \(f(x)=e^{\sin x}+e^{\cos x}\)
\(f^{\prime}(x)=0\)
\(\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow e^{\sin x} \cdot \cos x+e^{\cos x}(-\sin x)=0 \\
& \Rightarrow e^{\sin x-\cos x}=\tan x
\end{aligned}\)
\(\mathrm{x}=\pi / 4\) or in general \(\mathrm{x}=\mathrm{n} \pi+\frac{\pi}{4}\)
Now, \(f^{\prime \prime}(x)  < 0\) at \(x=\pi / 4\) or \(x=n \pi+\pi / 4\)
So, Global maximum exists at infinitely many points
